newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Top developments on Wednesday in Zaire crisis.
newsitem.headline: Top developments on Wednesday in Zaire crisis.

text.p: Following are top developments on Wednesday in the crisis in eastern Zaire:
--Efforts to help 1.2 million refugees stranded in the war zone reached stalemate as Zaire told aid agencies to keep out and the U.N. said many lives were at risk.
--In Madrid, a Foreign Ministry spokesman said Spain and France want to send a multinational force of at least 5,000 in a relief effort to open humanitarian corridors.
--But in Kinshasa, Zaire said it was asking aid agencies not to use its soil to distribute food for the refugees.
--In Brussels, European Union development ministers are to meet on Thursday to discuss aid for the refugees but will avoid discussing whether to intervene militarily to deliver it.
--In Paris, French President Jacques Chirac consulted senior officials as Paris disclosed that an envoy held secret talks with ailing Zairean leader Mobutu Sese Seko in Switzerland last week.
--In Nice, France, the U.N. envoy for the crisis, Raymond Chretien, arrived for talks at Mobutu's Riviera retreat.
--In Pretoria, South Africa said it had suspended a deal to supply arms worth about $18.5 million to the Rwandan government.
--In Addis Ababa, the Organisation of African Unity said a ministerial meeting of its 17-nation conflict prevention group would be held there next week to discuss the conflict.
